input.question: Hypothetically what is the worst thing that could happen if I don't turn on "airplane mode"?
input.ground_truth: Nothing. In 2015 alone, airplanes [carried ~3.441B people](_URL_0_). Most of them have devices with radios (phones, tablets, laptops). Many of them simply forgot to turn it off. There has never been a single malfunction of any sort attributed to a GSM/UMTS/LTE or WiFi radio not turned off. As a side note, FAA does not prohibit cellphone (much less WiFi) operation during flight, see 14 CFR 91.21 (b)(5); FCC and carriers do.

Question: Hypothetically what is the worst thing that could happen if I don't turn on "airplane mode"?

Answer:

response.prediction: Okay, let’s imagine your phone is like a little radio. When you’re on an airplane, if you don’t turn off the radio part (that’s what “airplane mode” does), your phone might try to talk to other phones or towers while you’re flying really high up. That could be like lots of radios talking at the same time and might bother the airplane or other phones on the ground. Also, your phone’s battery might run out faster because it’s working hard trying to find a signal. But the most important thing is to help keep everyone safe on the plane. So, turning on airplane mode is like being polite and helping the airplane do its job!
